text:
jason: Hey team — hitting 401 invalid_api_key repeatedly. Flow: our front-end requests a short-lived console token (issued by our IdP via SSO), then calls /v1/chat. First call succeeds, subsequent calls ~30-50s later get 401. Token TTL on the IdP is 60s. Any known timing/refresh issues?

anna: Sorry you're blocked — can you paste the exact curl you used and the error body? Also, is the client reusing the same TCP connection or opening a new one per request?

jason: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJld...short" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
HTTP/2 200
{ \"id\": \"resp_abc\", \"status\": \"ok\" }
... then after ~45s:
HTTP/2 401
{ \"error\": { \"type\": \"invalid_api_key\", \"message\": \"API key invalid or expired\", \"request_id\": \"req_20240301_42ab\" } }

lia: thanks — couple quick checks: 1) is the token you're creating a "console ephemeral session" (created via Console > Sessions) or a dashboard API key? 2) are you using fetch/keepalive/service worker that might reuse connections? 3) can you share the exact token creation time and any request_id from the 401?

jason: It's the console ephemeral session — created via the blue "Create session" button. Token creation time: 2024-03-01T18:12:05Z. 401 request_id: req_20240301_42ab. Frontend uses keep-alive and reuses a single websocket/tcp for multiple calls.

kevin: tagging in eng — short summary: console ephemeral sessions are intended for single-session/high-privilege interactive use and currently expire at 60s after issuance (we enforce expiry server-side). If the client reuses the same long-lived connection and the session token expires mid-connection, some HTTP/2 connection pools or proxies can keep routing requests incorrectly and result in 401s. :thinking:

kevin: two mitigation paths: 1) use a dashboard long-lived API key for background/long-lived HTTP calls; 2) implement token refresh: request a fresh session token before TTL and rotate Authorization header on the connection (or open a fresh connection after refresh). We're going to check if our token-expiry header is being propagated to edge caches.

anna: I've escalated to infra/edge. Created INC-1234. Can you attach the 401 request_id (gave it) and your org id? Also, as a quick repro, can you try setting Connection: close and retry to see if the failure still happens?

jason: Org: org_98765. Tried Connection: close — still saw a 401 on the second request but it was delayed slightly. Happy to run more tests.

deploy-bot: Deployed a small probe to edge token-checker in region us-west-2 to log token expiry mismatches (probe id: probe_6161).

kevin: From logs (grabbed by probe) we see console tokens are being marked expired ~60s after issuance and we're returning 401 correctly. There's a small window where multiplexed streams on HTTP/2 keep some state; we're adding a mitigation to invalidate streams when token expiry is near. ETA for patch: next deploy in 2–3 hours.

lia: For now, recommendation to customer: switch to a dashboard API key for non-interactive calls, or rotate tokens client-side every 45s. If you want, we can temporarily extend the console session TTL for your org while we roll the fix — need approval from security.

jason: Thanks — we'll switch to a dashboard key for now and let you know if we need the TTL extension. Appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:

anna: Closing loop: INC-1234 assigned to eng (kevin). Patch scheduled. We'll follow up in this thread with post-deploy results.
